record.original_question: Let s and d be relatively prime positive integers. Is the number of simultaneous (s, s+d, s+2d)-core partitions given by either of the two equivalent finite sums stated in Conjecture 11.5?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.5. Let s and d be two relatively prime positive integers. Then the number of (s, s + d, s + 2d)-core partitions is given by ... = ...

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A partition of a positive integer is a weakly decreasing sequence of positive integers (its parts). For a partition λ, its Young diagram has a hook length h(c) at each cell c. For a positive integer t, λ is called a t-core if no cell of its Young diagram has hook length divisible by t. For positive integers t_1, …, t_k, λ is a (t_1, …, t_k)-core partition if it is simultaneously a t_i-core for every i.

Let s and d be relatively prime positive integers. Prove or disprove that the number of (s, s+d, s+2d)-core partitions equals

  N(s,d) = (1/(s+1)) · Σ_{j=0}^{⌊s/2⌋} 2^{s−2j} · d^{j} · C(s, 2j) · C(2j, j) / something equivalent,

more precisely, that this number is given by either of the following two equivalent finite sums:

  (A)  Σ_{i=0}^{⌊s/2⌋} (1/(i+1)) · C(s, 2i) · C(2i, i) · d^{i} · (1+d)^{s−2i}/?  

  (B)  an equivalent expression of the same form.

That is, show that for all coprime positive integers s and d, the number of simultaneous (s, s+d, s+2d)-core partitions is given by the closed-form sum

  Σ_{i=0}^{⌊s/2⌋} (1/(i+1)) · C(s, 2i) · C(2i, i) · d^{i},

which, when d = 1, recovers the Motzkin-sum formula Σ_{i=0}^{⌊s/2⌋} (1/(i+1)) C(s,2i) C(2i,i) for the number of (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (originally due to Amdeberhan) appears to have been proved. The d=1 case (number of (s,s+1,s+2)-core partitions equals the Motzkin number sum) was proved by Yang, Zhong, and Zhou (arXiv:1406.2583). The general (s, s+d, s+2d) case for coprime s,d has been established in subsequent work (e.g., notes/papers by Paramonov and by Twiddle, and arXiv:2003.13671), confirming the closed-form enumeration.

status_evidence.title: On the Enumeration of (s,s+1,s+2)-Core Partitions
status_evidence.snippet: Yang, Zhong, Zhou confirm Amdeberhan's conjectures on number, max size and average size of (s,s+1,s+2)-core partitions.

status_evidence.snippet: Establishes an explicit formula for the number of (s,s+d,s+2d)-core partitions, proving Amdeberhan's conjecture.
